errors.what: “Estradiol and progesterone suppress GnRH, LH and FSH for most of the cycle.”
errors.why_wrong: This makes progesterone sound like a sustained regulator throughout the follicular phase, when its major rise and negative feedback occur after ovulation. The feedback varies by cycle phase.

errors.what: “Inhibin B from granulosa cells suppresses FSH only.”
errors.why_wrong: Its selective effect on FSH is correct, but presenting inhibin B as the inhibin feedback loop for the whole cycle omits inhibin A, which predominates in the luteal phase. See [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279054/).
The LH surge is the dominant response, but a smaller FSH surge also occurs at mid-cycle. The label can suggest FSH does not rise. See [Endotext](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279054/).

errors.what: The dotted inhibin arrow ends at the “Anterior pituitary” box.
errors.why_wrong: The arrow does not visually identify the FSH output as its selective target; that distinction relies on the nearby text.

errors.what: The diagram and legend occupy only the upper part of a tall image, with very small labels.
errors.why_wrong: The unused space makes the feedback labels and legend unnecessarily hard to read at the supplied size.

verdict: The main arrow directions and feedback relationships are sound, and the figure covers the caption. Phase-specific hormone roles and the smaller mid-cycle FSH surge need clearer treatment.
